memories.memory_text: I wait nervously in my Peugeot on a quiet street in a wealthy part of Paris, watching the shadows and wondering if anyone can see me.

grounded_facts: The group attempts to flee the scene in the Peugeot, but the car is trapped between vehicles and cannot pull out smoothly.
memories.memory_text: I tried to pull the Peugeot out, but there was barely any space between the Mercedes in front and the car behind, so I kept jerking back and forth like a pinball stuck between bumpers.

grounded_facts: Julien blames Raymond for not moving the car before they exited the house, expressing anger.
memories.memory_text: I was told I didn't think to move the car before we came out, and Julien was angry about it.

grounded_facts: The old man fires his shotgun at the Peugeot, shattering the left-side windows.
memories.memory_text: I saw the old man fire his shotgun at the Peugeot, and I ducked as the left-side windows shattered around us.

grounded_facts: Daniel urgently tells Raymond to get the car moving to escape the gunfire.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Daniel to get us out of there right away when the gunfire started.

grounded_facts: Raymond forcefully dislodges the Peugeot by accelerating into the Mercedes, enabling escape from the blocked alley.
memories.memory_text: I floored the Peugeot, revving the engine before releasing the brake and ramming into the Mercedes to push it out of the way so I could escape the alley.

grounded_facts: Daniel sees the old man running from his house with a shotgun, revealing immediate external threat.
memories.memory_text: I saw the old man firing his shotgun as I tried to free the car, and I realized we were in immediate danger, so I floored the Peugeot and rammed the Mercedes to get us out fast before he could take another shot.

grounded_facts: The immediate escape following a heist, taking place in a moving Peugeot at night, marked by rising internal conflict.
memories.memory_text: I was driving the Peugeot that night, right after the heist, and I could feel the tension building inside the car — we were moving but not really getting away, and everything started to unravel.

grounded_facts: The crew abandons the hallway and rushes back into their hotel suite to take cover.
memories.memory_text: I rushed back into our hotel suite with the crew to take cover from the gunfire in the hallway.

grounded_facts: An armed standoff and subsequent gunfight between the Wiseguys and the crew in a hotel hallway, interrupted by the presence of a civilian child.
memories.memory_text: I was in the hallway with Daniel, Marcel, and Zero when the Wiseguys showed up and we all went for our guns; then they started shooting and the whole place erupted in gunfire, so we had to rush back into our suite to take cover.

grounded_facts: The group gathers in a small cottage following a shooting; they attend to Zero's injury and share minimal food.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting at the table with the others in that small cottage after the shooting, and I remember Sami and me grimacing as we realized what they were about to do to Zero's wound.

grounded_facts: Zero makes a sexual joke about his anatomy while instructing Sami to be careful cutting his pants, lightening the mood despite his injury.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Zero made that crude joke about his anatomy while Sami was cutting his pants—he said to be careful because he has a very long one, and then winked. I could tell Sami was unsettled by how casually Zero joked despite being shot, and I grimaced alongside Sami, feeling the tension in the room.

grounded_facts: Sami sprays cheese whiz from a can onto bread, presenting it as food, which the French men react to with disbelief.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sami spray cheese from a can onto bread like it was normal food, and I couldn't believe it—none of us could. We all looked at him like he was from another planet, and even I could feel how wrong it seemed, like something wasn't right about that 'cheese'.

grounded_facts: Daniel uses a red-hot tire wrench to cauterize Zero's wound after removing the tourniquet and pouring vodka on the injury.
memories.memory_text: I saw Daniel release the tourniquet and pour vodka on Zero's wound before Marcel pressed the red-hot tire wrench to it, and I could see Zero trying not to scream from the pain.

grounded_facts: Raymond brings up the release of new Beaujolais wine in France and engages Sami in a conversation about alcohol preferences, which Sami interprets as an attempt to distract from recent traumatic events.
memories.memory_text: I brought up the new Beaujolais release in France to start a conversation about drinks, and when Sami mentioned preferring Glenmorangie, I acknowledged it was good—I just wanted to shift focus away from everything we'd been through, and I felt relieved when he agreed to share a glass with me later.

grounded_facts: Raymond visits Vinny Zammito at his house during the day to deliver a proposition regarding financial assistance.
memories.memory_text: I visited Vinny at his house during the day and knocked on his door, which he answered with his arm in a sling.

grounded_facts: Raymond offers Vinny an Impala as a gift on behalf of an anonymous person, intended to help with his financial problems.

memories.memory_text: I told Vinny the Impala was his as a gift from an anonymous benefactor, and I suggested he could give it to his brother or anyone he owes money to as partial payment to help with his financial problems.

grounded_facts: Sami, Marcel, Raymond, and Zero arrive at the private airport and assist Zero toward a small plane.
memories.memory_text: I helped Sami and Marcel get Zero out of the taxi and walk him toward the small plane.

grounded_facts: A coordinated effort at a private airport to prepare Zero's departure to Canada, involving a transaction between Daniel and Bonanno.
memories.memory_text: I could tell there was some kind of deal happening between Daniel and Bonanno, but I didn't know the full details—something about half the tapes and the rest still being out there.

grounded_facts: Bastaldi steps outside and notices Daniel, Sami, Raymond, Marcel, and Zero standing across the street, staring at him.
memories.memory_text: I was standing with Daniel, Sami, Marcel, and Zero across the street from Bastaldi, staring at him so he'd notice us.

grounded_facts: After being momentarily blocked from view by a bus, the crew disappears and is revealed to be crouched behind a parked car, observing Bastaldi's reaction.
memories.memory_text: I crouched behind a parked car with the crew after the bus passed, watching Bastaldi try to figure out where we'd gone.

grounded_facts: Raymond asks what Bastaldi is doing, and Marcel replies that he is looking for them.
memories.memory_text: I asked what Bastaldi was doing, and Marcel told me he was looking for us.

grounded_facts: Zero expresses that he cannot remain in hiding much longer due to his injured leg causing pain.
memories.memory_text: I heard Zero say he couldn't stay in hiding much longer because his leg was hurting.

grounded_facts: Marcel retrieves a case containing stacks of five hundred franc notes from the rowboat, indicating the successful acquisition of significant funds.
memories.memory_text: I saw Marcel retrieve the case from the rowboat and open it, revealing stacks of five hundred franc notes, which meant we had the money.

grounded_facts: After retrieving the money, Marcel looks at Raymond with a grin and nods, signaling mutual understanding or approval.
memories.memory_text: I remember Marcel looking at me with a grin and nodding, and I understood it was his way of acknowledging our success together.

grounded_facts: Raymond opens his cell phone, suggesting an intention to initiate communication following the retrieval of the money.
memories.memory_text: I opened my cell phone, ready to make the call now that I had the money.

grounded_facts: A group gathers across the river after destroying the tapes to observe the wreckage and inspect the payment.
memories.memory_text: I was with the group across the river, watching the smoldering wreckage after we destroyed the tapes.

grounded_facts: The group discovers that the suitcase contains mostly fake money, with only the top bill of each stack being real.
memories.memory_text: I opened the suitcase and saw that only the top bill of each stack was real, with fake paper underneath, so I realized the money was mostly counterfeit.

grounded_facts: Daniel challenges Marcel for failing to verify the contents of the money suitcase.
memories.memory_text: I heard Daniel challenge Marcel for not verifying what was in the money suitcase.

grounded_facts: The group walks across a bridge, during which major conflicts and discoveries occur.
memories.memory_text: I walked across the bridge with the others, and that's where everything started to fall apart.

grounded_facts: Marcel apologizes and acknowledges he made a mistake by not checking the money, which led to their loss.
memories.memory_text: I heard Marcel apologize, admitting he made a mistake by not checking the money, which cost us everything.

grounded_facts: Raymond suddenly shouts at Marcel, calling him a moron and expressing intense frustration over the money mistake.
Raymond verbally lashes out at Marcel, calling him a moron and a stupid shit-head for not checking the money.
memories.memory_text: I suddenly shouted at Marcel, calling him a moron and a stupid shit-head because I couldn't believe he didn't check the money—it was such a critical mistake.

grounded_facts: Marcel demands that Sami give him the baseball, asserting ownership due to having taken it.
memories.memory_text: I heard Marcel demand the baseball from Sami, claiming it was his because he was the one who took it, and then telling Sami to give it to him.

grounded_facts: During a physical struggle over the bag, it rips and the baseball rolls off the bridge into the river.
memories.memory_text: I saw the bag rip during the struggle between Marcel and Sami, and the baseball rolled off the bridge into the river.

grounded_facts: Sami refuses Marcel's demand to return the baseball, asserting it is not his to take.
Sami asserts ownership of the autographed baseball, rejecting Marcel's claim and preventing him from taking it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sami refuse to give the baseball to Marcel, shouting that he wasn't entitled to it and pulling the bag away when Marcel tried to take it.

grounded_facts: The torn lining of the canvas bag exposes Van Gogh's 'Vase with Twelve Sunflowers', previously hidden.
memories.memory_text: I saw the torn lining of the canvas bag reveal Van Gogh's 'Vase with Twelve Sunflowers'—it had been hidden there all along.

grounded_facts: As the group moves toward the painting, a passing truck's wind lifts it over the railing and into the river.
memories.memory_text: I rushed toward the painting with the others, but as we got close, a passing truck's wind lifted it over the railing and I watched it fall into the river.

memories.memory_text: I told Julien to be careful with the lighter—right as he grabbed it, I saw it burn his hand and fly into the curtains.
I handed the canvas to Julien, and he used it to beat the flames. The canvas caught fire, and after he put it out, I saw the painting was ruined.
I told Raymond to steal a car because using Sophie's would leave a traceable license plate, and I needed this job done clean and quiet.

I remember snapping at Sophie when I realized she gave us the wrong address—'That moron'—and then cutting off the excuses by telling the crew to get some sleep and that we were leaving in the morning.

I grabbed the cassette from the deck and played it—Zammito’s voice came through, talking about taking down Bonanno like it was nothing. I remember the weight of the tape in my hand, the silence in the room as we all realized this wasn’t just a heist.

After the tape ended, I said we couldn’t just run—stealing money is one thing, but these recordings make us targets. I could feel the panic rising, but I kept my voice steady because someone had to keep control.
I told Hadley I'd have Zero shoot him in the knee, and when he didn't back down, I gave the nod—Zero's gun was already aimed, waiting for my signal.
I remember shouting that Bastaldi was dead, really dead, and that I was going to kill him myself—no more running, no more deals, just blood.

I called Lamar to confirm the escape setup, and when he tried to jack up the price because of the news coverage, I didn't waste time arguing—said fine and hung up. Ten o'clock at the Barclay, room 211, and the line went dead.
I handed Lamar the envelope and told him there was ten grand in it—his for keeping his head down and doing what I said.
I looked at him and said, 'I'll tell you when it's time,' making sure he knew I was the one calling the shots.
I picked up the phone and heard Sami's voice—urgent, no greeting—telling me to get out, that company was coming up. The line went dead fast, but the warning hit hard.
I told Raymond to grab the tapes and that we were leaving—no time for debate—but he just argued back, asking why he had to do it. I couldn't believe it, had to move fast and grab the bag myself.
I stood in the doorway with my gun raised, watching Hadley's face go pale when he saw us—just a split second before we took control.
I cuffed Hadley to the pipe under the sink with his own cuffs—solid leverage, no easy way out.
The second we stepped into the hallway, everything went to hell—guns drawn on both sides, and that little girl just standing there in her pink dress before Marcel tackled her down.
I saw the lock on the adjoining door and fired my gun to blow it off—told the crew to move through. No time to explain, just get out.
I ran forward under fire, both guns blazing, and threw the spare to Marcel—saw it spin through the air in slow motion before it hit him in the head.
After the gun throw, I fired a few shots to push the wiseguy back, then grabbed Zero with Marcel and hauled him to the car while bullets cracked around us.

I used my belt as a tourniquet on Zero, told Sami to bring scissors, and had Raymond cut Zero's pants up the leg. I poured vodka over the wound and used a towel to pick up the tire iron from the stove before walking back to the bed.

Sami sprayed cheese from a can onto bread like it meant nothing, and all of us just stared—he didn’t get it. I said 'Thank God' when he said you couldn’t do that in France, but it wasn’t about the cheese; it was the absurdity of eating at all while Zero lay there waiting to be burned alive.
I stood at the door and said I wanted to see Bonanno, and when that didn't work, I told Half Tooth Tony I was the one who robbed Frankie Zammito.
I played the tape of Zammito talking about overthrowing Bonanno, watching his face tighten with rage as the truth sank in.
I refused to give Bonanno our location, just told him I'd call him when he needed to reach me—no favors, no leverage.
I pulled out the roll of bills and told Lamar there was one more thing I needed him to do—he started to protest, but then he saw the money and shut up, said 'I'm listening.'
I was on the phone with Mr. Bonanno in the taxi, asking him something—couldn’t say what exactly—and he agreed. I just said thanks and hung up.
I handed Bonanno the cassette case with half the tapes, and he passed it to Half Tooth Tony to check—when Tony confirmed they were good, I told Bonanno I'd destroy the rest, and he had my word.

I stood across the street from Bastaldi, just watching him—letting him see us, letting him feel the weight of it before we vanished behind the car. When he turned back inside, I knew we’d won without saying a word.

I called Bastaldi from the shadows and told him I had the tapes—he started stammering about not having a million, but I cut him off, reminding him I know about the Van Gogh; his voice cracked when he said Vincent got arrested before bringing it back.
I watched Bastaldi step onto the deck, place the suitcase in the rowboat, and cut it loose—the current took it slow at first, just like I said it would.
I pressed the button on the detonator, feeling the weight of it—this was for Julien.

memories.memory_text: I called Daniel out for almost getting his ass blown off, then shut Raymond down when he tried to act smart—I don’t care about his 'Black Panther' crap, and I sure as hell didn’t ask for his therapy session.
I told Raymond to get on his knees and 'communicate with my dick'—Bastaldi had to step in, but I wasn’t backing down. I wasn’t there to talk feelings, I was there to make sure we followed orders.
I stepped in and saw Sami trying to bolt—caught him turning back with that fake smile. I just looked at him and said, 'Going somewhere?'
He said he didn't have the money, but I wasn't there to talk. I opened the bathroom door and shoved him in—no hesitation.
I punched Sami in the gut and slammed the bathroom door when that big guy walked in—he didn’t know what was really going down, but I made sure he didn’t stick around to find out.
I told Sami he’s going to Chicago with the crew—if he runs, I’ll find him and cut him up in a bathroom next time. Then I handed him the paper with the address.

I stepped out of the limo and saw the surprise on Daniel’s face—he didn’t expect me, not as the one watching him. When he snapped, 'You don't trust me?', I felt the edge in the air, the shift in control.
I changed the station from that Renaud crap to Hallyday—mine was better, and I could see Zero hating it, so I knew I’d won a point.
After Bastaldi shut it off and glared at me, I started singing 'que je t'aime' low—just enough for Zero to hear, not enough for him to stop me.
I knocked on the door and said we were looking for Sophie — Laurant sent us. That was all it took.
I saw Raymond slink in like a wet dog, head down, and I felt the anger rise—Daniel gave me that look, just a nod, and I knew it was time to go.
I head butted him hard, felt my forehead crack into the bridge of his nose—he dropped his hands, blood already gushing.
I grabbed his hair and kept punching him in the face, driving him backward into the room with each hit.

I felt the punch from behind, bent my head down, and heard his knuckles crack. Then I kneed him in the groin, kicked the back of his knee, and elbowed him in the head. He went down face first and didn't move.
I turned toward the one by the stereo—smaller, already scared—and he shut it off without a word. Just silence after that.
I walked in and Wayne asked what I said to them. I told him nothing.
I remember saying the map said to go left, and then Julien flipped it around—suddenly it was obvious we’d been holding it wrong. I couldn’t help but laugh at that.
I stood in the shadows with Sami and Daniel, watching Julien work the alarm—numbers flashing on his device until he punched in the code and gave the signal.
I said I wanted to be Elvis—Sami tried to take it, but I pushed back and he gave in. I looked more like him anyway.
I saw that autographed baseball on the shelf, called it out, and tossed it in the bag—Daniel gave me a look, but I told him it was for my nephew.
I opened the safe expecting jewels, but there was nothing but stacks of cash and some envelopes—no jewels at all. I couldn't believe it; I kept saying there had to be more.

Sami pulled me aside and said we were in the wrong house—that the man we tied up was Frankie Zammito, the Underboss of the Chicago Mafia. I didn't recognize him at first, and then everything went cold when it hit me.
I said 'It's Elvis...' into the phone, then corrected myself—'It's me...'—knowing Bastaldi wouldn't like the hesitation, but the silence on the other end told me he was already suspicious.
I leaned in close to Daniel and asked him if he thought it was smart to tell Zammito we're French—our cover was already thin, and he just handed them more.
Bastaldi told me over the phone to take what we had and get out—his voice was sharp, then the line just went dead.
I climbed over the fence fast, right after the others, keeping my eyes forward—no time to look back, just move.
I said it was an honest mistake—Ridgeway, Ridgeroad, the names are close. I could feel the anger in the room, but I had to cut it off before it turned on us.
I grabbed Raymond and pulled him back to the car—no time for goodbyes, not with Ruiz and Zammito already hunting us.

Daniel asked if I knew about Bastaldi's deal with Zammito. I said no. He didn't believe me, like I'd ever help that man. I told him if Bastaldi had said he was stealing Van Gogh's 'Sunflowers in a vase,' I'd remember it.
Daniel called me a lap dog and an ass-kisser, pushing me in French like he always does — I told him he was testing my patience, and when he stepped toward me, I was ready to hit him.
I suggested giving the tapes back, trying to find a way out before things got worse, but Zero shut it down hard.
I lunged forward and tackled the girl to the ground just as the Wiseguys started drawing their guns.
I grabbed the girl and pulled her into her room while bullets were tearing up the hallway.
I handed the girl to her mother—she was shaking, eyes wide—but I didn’t stop. No time for reunions.
I shot the lock off the adjoining door and went through—no hesitation, just metal giving way and then silence on the other side.
I fired until my gun clicked empty, just trying to keep those Wiseguys down so Zero wouldn’t get hit again.
Something hard smacked me in the head—next thing I knew, it was Daniel’s gun flying at me, knocked me flat before I could catch it.

I said we should go in through the bedroom window after the outside alarm's down—Daniel agreed, and they started planning the rest around it.
I asked when we were going, and when Sophie said tonight, I shot back about jet lag—felt like the plan was moving too fast.
I told Sophie I got the tattoo in prison and served three years—then said she was married to my best friend when I got out. I didn’t want to say it, but it just came out.
She touched my arm, traced the tattoo, then smiled and said only 'the lucky ones' would see her tattoo if it was on her ass. I didn’t know what to say, just watched her walk away.
I leaned out of the Impala with the map in my hand, trying to make sense of where we were while talking to the attendant—streetlights flickering overhead, the paper edge curling in my grip.
I saw the name on the plaque—Frankie Zammito—and then I looked at his face, really looked, and the blood just left my body. When our eyes met, I knew we were in way over our heads.

I found the cassette tapes in a small cardboard box inside the canvas bag from Zammito’s safe. I took the box to the stereo and put one tape in the deck to see what a mob guy thought was worth locking up.
Sophie came in, said she could think of something better to do—then kissed me. I didn’t pull away, but I remember the weight of it, how the moment shifted and I wasn’t thinking about tapes anymore.
I woke up and looked to my side—Sophie wasn't there. Wayne said she left with a bag, and something in my gut tightened before I even knew why.
I ran to the table—the bag was gone. I turned to Daniel, shaking him awake, my voice sharp: 'Get up. We've been ripped off!'
I remembered the tape I'd left in the deck last night—Sophie didn't take it. I pulled it out, suddenly aware I might be the only one who knew it was still here.
When Zammito's voice came through the speakers talking about taking down Bonanno, I froze—this wasn't just a theft anymore. I had to quiet the others so I could hear every word.
I tried to play it cool, told the clerk I thought the woman checking in was having an affair—same tired line that works in half the fleabags from Marseille to Belgrade. He didn’t bite.
I came back with Zero. Didn’t say a word—just stood there while he put the gun under the guy’s jaw. The second that metal touched skin, the room number spilled out.
I knocked, and the second she started to open it, I shoved the door hard—felt it hit something behind it, probably her, but I didn’t look. I stepped in fast, shoulder first.
I touched the wires from the lamp to Hadley's hand and watched him jerk and scream—then he finally admitted they'd been using us to get Zammito's tapes.
I asked Sophie what she was getting out of it, and she just said 'Money'—no hesitation, no regret, like betraying us was just another job.

I stared at Sophie, jaw tight. Laurant and Vincent Bastaldi were working with Zammito, replacing real paintings like Van Gogh's 'Vase with twelve sunflowers' with copies. The originals went to Paris to be sold. I could only ask, 'Why?'

Hadley’s voice cut through the room—calm, knowing—saying if we walked out, we’d have both the FBI and Zammito’s people hunting us. I felt the weight of the bag, the door, the walls closing in. No way out.
I corrected Marcel—it's "Vase with twelve Sunflowers," not "Sunflowers in a vase." He brushed it off, but the title mattered; getting it wrong showed he didn't know the score.
I stepped between Marcel and Daniel when they moved toward each other—fists tense, voices sharp in French. I told them to knock it off; we didn’t have time for their shit.
I shut Julien down when he started panicking—told him he wasn't helping, got right in his face so he'd stop spiraling. We didn't have time for his meltdown.
I said it doesn't matter where we run—Zammito and the FBI will track us down no matter what, so we have to face it here, even if I don’t know how yet.

I saw a guy in the lobby who looked just like Raymond—same build, same walk—and when I bumped into him, I slid his wallet out clean. Felt the weight of it in my hand for just a second before tucking it away.
I dialed the number, paper in hand, and asked Hadley if he knew who he was talking to—then set the meet for Grant Park, one hour, by the statue.
I stepped out and shouted at Hadley—he set me up, that piece of shit—and then he slammed me against the statue, started searching me like I was some common criminal.

I asked what I'd get for the tapes, and when he said a 'pass,' I pushed back—there's a witness who can place me at the scene—then he told me they don't have the murder weapon, that he has it, the lamp with my prints and her blood, and held up his burned hand like it meant something.
I realized right then he wasn't just dirty—he was selling the tapes to vanish with the money, like some fat rat jumping off a sinking ship.
When he said Sophie had to die because she was a loose end, and looked at me like I was next, I knew he'd kill me too once I handed over the tapes.
I saw Raymond come in—limping, torn up, not saying a word—and when Daniel asked about Julien, he just shook his head. I didn’t need to hear it out loud.
I said it plain—Zero was right, the tapes give us leverage. That’s when I knew we weren’t just running anymore.
I swapped the bag with the tapes while the others were asleep and the shower was running—quiet, clean, no one saw me move.
